title: Plugin Sandbox Hardening and Scheduler Contract
author: Lina Chen
content:
Summary
This document defines the security and isolation model for runtime plugins ("extension modules"), the scheduler contract that governs plugin execution and preemption, and operational guidance for hardening, profiling and benchmarking plugin-enabled runtime paths. It is intended for runtime engineers, SRE, and security reviewers.

Goals
- Allow safe, resource-bounded extensions to the serving runtime (e.g., custom token preprocessors, routing adapters, feature gates) while preserving tenant isolation and SLOs.
- Define a clear scheduler contract so plugin authors and kernel/scheduler teams share expectations about CPU/GPU/IO budgets, preemption, and observable signals.
- Specify profiling and benchmarking methodology for plugin-enabled experiments to avoid blind spots in latency/cost analyses.

Scope
- Applies to: ephemeral plugins loaded into the runtime process or per-request sandboxes (WASM, subprocess, container), scheduler hooks that influence kernel selection, and the profiling/canary paths used during deploys.
- Excludes: long-lived persistent sidecars with separate process governance (see appendix for cross-process patterns).

Definitions
- Plugin: a modular extension that executes during various stages of request processing (preprocess, postprocess, routing).
- Sandbox: the isolation boundary for a plugin (WASM runtime, seccomp + cgroup, or container).
- Execution slot: logical budget allocated by the scheduler for a plugin invocation (time + CPU + GPU hints + ephemerality flag).
- Kernel: the runtime component that executes model inference.

Security & Isolation Model (high level)
1) Default isolation: all third-party or untrusted plugins must run in a sandboxed environment. Approved internal plugins may run in-process only after security review and feature-flag gating.
2) Resource cgroups: every sandboxed plugin invocation must be instantiated with a cgroup (CPU quota, memory limit, blkio throttle). Suggested defaults are in the config table below.
3) Syscall filters: use seccomp policies tailored to each sandbox type; prohibit network access unless explicitly requested and approved.
4) Filesystem access: sandboxes must mount read-only data volumes; write access limited to ephemeral tmpfs with size caps.
5) Cryptographic keys: plugin code must not receive plaintext customer keys. Any KMS/HSM access must be proxied by a runtime RPC that performs auth checks and enforces audit logging.
6) Network egress: deny by default. Egress rules require an allowlist and audit trail (team + ticket id).

Recommended cgroup defaults (table)
| parameter | recommended default | rationale |
|-----------|--------------------:|----------|
| cpu_quota | 100ms per invocation | bounds CPU tail latency when many small plugin calls occur |
| memory_limit | 64MB | prevents per-request memory blowups; increase only with review |
| blkio_weight | 50 (out of 1000) | limits disk pressure from plugins during retries or dumps |
| pids_max | 32 | prevents fork bombs from exhausting node resources |
| ephemeral_tmp_size | 8MB | prevents uncontrolled temp file growth |

Scheduler contract (concise)
- Scheduler shall advertise per-invocation execution slots with the following attributes: {slot_id, cpu_budget_ms, wall_time_deadline_ms, priority_class, preemptible:true/false, affinity_hint}. Plugin runtime must accept these attributes at start and enforce budget locally.
- Plugins must check remaining_budget_ms on each yield point (documented below) and abort gracefully returning a standardized status: "plugin.timeout" or "plugin.preempted".
- Preemption semantics: when the scheduler reclaims a slot, the plugin process/wasm runtime must receive a soft-signal (SIGUSR1-equivalent) and begin controlled shutdown within soft_shutdown_ms (default 20ms). If soft shutdown does not complete, the hard-kill path triggers after hard_kill_ms (default 150ms).
- Affinity and locality: plugins that request GPU hints must annotate affinity_hint; the scheduler may reject or remap hints to keep kernel scheduling deterministic.

Plugin lifecycle and API checklist
1. Manifest: every plugin bundle must include a manifest.yaml with: name, version, author, declared_api_surface (pre/post/routing), declared_resource_hints, required_capabilities (network, file_write), and signing_checksum. Example manifest snippet: 

manifest.yaml
---
name: redwood.token-filter
version: 0.3.1
author: internal:token-team
api: [preprocess]
resource_hints:
  cpu_ms: 20
  memory_mb: 16
capabilities: [network:false, file_write:false]
signature: "sha256:..."

2. Signing & provenance: plugin bundles must be signed by an approved build pipeline. The runtime verifies the signature against a rotation-aware public key list at load time.
3. Static analysis: run the plugin through the sandbox-targeted static analyzer (see pipeline job: eng-serving-runtime/plugin-static-check).
4. Canary: deploy plugin in a canary with 1% of traffic, run the profiling and tail-latency checks described later, and only escalate to broader rollout after meeting SLOs for 48 hours.

Yield points and cooperative preemption
- Yield points are the only safe locations where user code may check budgets: after deserialize, after tokenization, and before issuing kernel offload. For WASM plugins, provide a host function check_budget() which returns remaining_budget_ms and allows early return.
- Cooperative window: plugin code must assume that a hard preemption may occur at any syscall boundary; keep critical sections small and idempotent.

Observability & Profiling requirements
- Telemetry emitted per invocation: plugin.id, invocation.id, slot_id, start_ts, end_ts, cpu_ms_user, cpu_ms_sys, memory_peak_mb, decision_trace (max 512 chars), status.
- Traces: span naming convention: runtime.plugin.<plugin-name>.<phase>. Include kernel hint tags when applicable.
- Sampling: for production, sample all plugin failures and 0.5% of successful calls; during canary increase sampling to 100% for the first 10k invocations or 24h.
- Profiling: capture wall time + CPU time histograms; keep p90/p99 deltas before and after plugin enablement as part of the benchmark report.

Benchmark & Canary checklist (step-by-step)
1) Baseline: run a 24h synthetic run of the target workload without the plugin. Capture per-route p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost-per-token.
2) Synthetic plugin run: enable plugin on a shadow copy of traffic at 0x cost impact and measure overhead with production kernels.
3) Canary rollout: 1% traffic (multi-az). Monitor plugin metrics + runtime SLOs for 48h. Key thresholds: p99 increase <= 5% absolute and error-rate increase <= 0.1 percentage points.
4) Scale test: run a 6-hour stress with burst emulation (2x normal peak) and validate eviction and preemption paths.
5) Postmortem criteria: if any kernel timeouts, oom-kill, or scheduler-induced rollbacks occur, halt rollout and run rollback checklist.

Runbook: plugin-induced latency spike (operational steps)
1) Detection: alert fires for route X when p99 > baseline + 5% sustained for 2 minutes.
2) Immediate mitigation: disable plugin routing flag for affected route (CLI: rwdctl runtime plugin disable --route X --plugin name).
3) Trace collection: snapshot last 500 traces with trace-ids tagged plugin=true and upload to /var/tmp/plugin-triage/<inc_id>.
4) Revert decision: if disabling returns SLOs to normal within 3 minutes, keep disabled and create P0 incident. If no change, escalate to scheduler oncall.
5) Post-incident: run the profiling checklist and attach findings to incident record.

Runbook: plugin resource runaway (memory or cpu)
1) Pager triggers on node-level oom_kill or cpu_throttle > 70% sustained.
2) Isolate: scheduler should mark node as cordoned_for_plugins and start draining plugin-invocations to new nodes.
3) Kill policy: notify plugin owner_team via automated page; issue soft-kill to plugin processes and escalate to hard kill after hard_kill_ms.
4) Recovery: autoscale replacement nodes if needed and run kernel-level health checks.

Hardening checklist for security review
- Ensure manifest signature validated and build provenance recorded.
- Verify seccomp/capabilities are the minimal set for declared features.
- Confirm no direct KMS keys are provisioned into plugin environment.
- Run fuzzing for 72h using the runtime plugin-fuzz harness (job: eng-serving-runtime/plugin-fuzz-72h).
- Confirm telemetry contains at least 8 fields listed in Observability section and uses redaction policy for PII.

Example scheduler-policy fragment (YAML)
---
policy_name: plugin-defaults
priority_classes:
  - name: latency-sensitive
    cpu_budget_ms: 50
    preemptible: false
  - name: background
    cpu_budget_ms: 100
    preemptible: true
hard_kill_ms: 150
soft_shutdown_ms: 20
max_concurrent_plugins_per_node: 64

Testing harness commands
- Build and sign plugin: tools/plugin_builder --build ./pkg --sign --key-id ci-plugin-key-02
- Run unit sandbox locally: tools/sandbox_runner --bundle ./out/redwood.token-filter.tar.gz --profile debug --max-invocations 1000
- Canary enable: rwdctl runtime plugin enable --plugin redwood.token-filter --route reviews-api --percent 1 --reason "canary token-filter v0.3.1"

Ownership & SLA
- Plugin runtime and scheduler teams own the enforcement code and telemetry emitters.
- Plugin authoring teams own their manifests, static analysis fixes, and canary configuration.
- SLOs preserved: no plugin deploy should increase route p99 by more than 5% absolute or add >0.1pp error-rate without explicit senior eng approval.

Appendix A: Cross-process plugin patterns
If a plugin requires long-lived resources or external network egress, prefer a separate service with an authenticated, audited RPC. The RPC should be rate-limited and expose a per-request cost budget. This pattern isolates faults and allows independent scaling.

Appendix B: Troubleshooting quick reference
- Symptom: plugin not starting under cgroup -> check journalctl for cgroup OOM messages and policy mis-match in manifest.resource_hints.
- Symptom: plugin preempted frequently -> increase cpu_budget_ms in manifest for canary only and surface details via trace.
- Symptom: signature verification failed -> validate the public key rotation list and confirm the plugin bundle was built in the approved CI job.
